claims.text: Build-chamber preheating during LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi reduces thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients minimize residual stresses in LPBF-built AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced thermal gradients minimize microstructural heterogeneity.
Lower residual stress and microstructural heterogeneity improve mechanical performance relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
A build-chamber preheat of approximately 400–500 °C is an applicable processing window for AlCrFeNiSi.
Miniature AlCrFeNiSi components of approximately 5×5×5 mm can be fabricated by LPBF in an inert atmosphere while holding laser and scan parameters constant apart from chamber temperature.
Reduced thermal gradients lower the induced dislocation density.
Moderating rapid thermal contraction between successive layers minimizes localized microcracking.
Build-chamber preheating decreases the temperature difference between deposited layers and the substrate.
Reduced thermal shock slows rapid cooling and solidification.
Slower cooling and solidification limit the formation of high residual stresses.
Slower cooling and solidification limit microstructural defects that compromise mechanical properties.
Preheated components will have measurably lower X-ray-diffraction residual stresses than ambient-build components.
Preheated components will have improved ductility relative to ambient-build components.
Preheated components will have more uniform strength and hardness than ambient-build components.
Standard LPBF at ambient build temperature typically produces significant residual stresses.
Standard LPBF at ambient build temperature typically produces degraded mechanical properties.
Rapid thermal cycling in standard LPBF increases processing complexity.
The intervention is applicable only where preheating does not trigger unwanted phase transformations or oxidation.
The intervention requires sufficiently controlled heat dissipation in small AlCrFeNiSi components.
